US Offers $20 Million Reward for Iran Nuclear Intelligence

The State Department’s Rewards for Justice program is offering up to $20 million, along with possible relocation, for information about Iran’s nuclear program, U.S. Central Command announced Friday on
X

Rewards for Justice is offering a reward of up to $20 million and possible relocation for information about Iran’s nuclear program, including its facilities, equipment, and associated personnel, such as those in the scientific community, or the movement of any of the above.…
The offer covers intelligence about nuclear facilities, equipment and associated personnel, including members of Iran’s scientific community.

The State Department said Iran’s failure to meet its safeguards obligations to the International Atomic Energy Agency has left the watchdog without a complete picture of the country’s centrifuge production and inventory.
The loss of what the agency calls “continuity of knowledge” has complicated efforts to track Iran’s nuclear activities.
The U.S. government remains committed to countering any attempt by Iran to develop a nuclear weapons program.
If you have information on Iran’s nuclear personnel or technologies, send us a tip.
Trump Repeats Claims of Destroying Iran’s Nuclear Program
The reward announcement comes despite President Trump’s repeated assertions that U.S. military strikes effectively eliminated Iran’s nuclear capabilities.
“If we didn’t hit Iran, you wouldn’t have Israel today,” Trump said Friday, arguing that Tehran would have devastated the Middle East if it had acquired nuclear weapons, ABC reported.
However, Trump also suggested that negotiations were progressing, saying that Iran was eager to end the conflict. “We’re dealing with them now. They want to make a deal very badly,” he said.
